# Contact-aware compliance acquisition: exact conditional interface

This construction is a mathematical acquisition-to-decision interface for a
specified dilute crack model. No component measurement, contact-class bound,
finite-component correction, or nondestructive protocol has been acquired.
The underlying open/closed differential-compliance measurement is established
prior art. The new work here is the derived contact-weighted matrix bound and
its executable conservative service calculation. Novelty of that combination
is UNKNOWN.

## Contract and provenance

Input: generalized tangent-compliance measurements at two uniform preloads;
deterministic entrywise errors; a bound on all load-dependent material,
fixture, finite-boundary, interaction, and model errors; and independently
supported coverage/contact conditions below. Output: an upper bound on the
largest isolated-crack Mode-I service stress intensity, for arbitrary crack
count and depths in a supplied compact interval. Costs: eight load settings
per two-preload/two-mode central-difference acquisition, displacement and
rotation sensing, plus the calibration/model evidence. The numerical
certificate itself uses two-dimensional rational matrix algebra, monotone
scalar inversion and one-dimensional interval subdivision. No flaw image,
crack-count inference or pristine specimen is an input.

Primary exact elasticity source: Nishioka, Zhou & Fujimoto (2008), *On the
General Solutions for Mixed-Mode Penny-Shaped Crack and Their Applications*,
DOI [10.1299/jcst.2.34](https://doi.org/10.1299/jcst.2.34), full pinned PDF in
`sources/Nishioka2008.pdf`. Its uniform Mode-I SIF is Eq46, and the affine
bending result is §3.3/Eq60 (printed p43). Its infinite, homogeneous, isotropic
solid is the elasticity scope used here. The affine opening below is the
ordinary penny-crack solution; the source's tip coefficient independently
checks its factor 2/3. The energy integrals, contact variational bound and
decision interface below are derived here.

Peer convention: normal x; z is thickness coordinate; H is full thickness;
r=2z/H. Generalized loads p=(p0,p1) produce nominal axial stress p0+p1*r;
p0=F/A and p1=M_b*H/(2I). Conjugate coordinates are
q=(A*u_end, (2I/H)*theta_end). Each modeled crack is an internal circular
zero-thickness disk, normal x, radius a, center r. Cracks do not interact.
The material is linear elasti

# Accepted internal contact-aware acquisition reduction

The operator construction, measured-error reduction and continuous-depth certificate in `../../compliance_acquisition_bridge/PRIMARY_PROOF.md` are accepted at their stated isolated-disk/contact-model scope. The parent read the full proof, complete used core and driver, saved-leaf verifier, and final geometry/acquisition corrections. Frozen proof SHA-256 is `c411143dcb31ca81e47a38afa7b0d95544954846dad4c45b7e023c48f3121b82`; core is `b939456d3d52e104c726626f995d288d47e4e231acfc4eedd2b935de5cac3646`.

This is a substantive mathematical acceptance. For the open positive compliance operator C and a supplied normal-contact operator K>=kI, resolvent monotonicity and the restricted inverse variational principle give

`B* [C-(C^-1+K)^-1] B >= Q(Q+N/k)^-1 Q`,

where `Q=B*CB`, `N=B*B`. The parent checked the full chain, including its infinite-dimensional coercive inverse interpretation. The actual finite-disk energy gives the positive `8/(15H^2) sum(a^5)` bending term. Dropping the remaining positive gradient term yields the contact-weighted rank-one contribution

`h_k(a) v(r)v(r)^T`, with `h_k(a)=a^3*beta*k*a/(pi+beta*k*a)`.

Its strict monotonicity, positivity, measured-entry/nuisance Loewner inflation, individual inverse-matrix bound and conservative continuous-depth upper computations are valid. They cover any unknown finite population in the typed model, without identifying individual flaws or a minimum radius. The API checks matrix positivity, service all-open margin and sufficient burial in the thickness. Lateral burial and finite-component/model admission remain external obligations.

The parent constructed a different exact verification: `independent_box.py` imports no worker inverse, optimizer, square-root or saved output. It proves the pi bracket with rational Machin series, reconstructs the physical moment upper, and partitions the entire radius/depth rectangle, excluding infeasible cells by a contact-moment lower bound or certifying `K^2 < (5 MPa sqrt(m))^2` directly. # Contact-weighted compliance acquisition bridge

**Completed:** a conditional, executable map from an imperfect open/closed
compliance contrast to a bound on the largest crack's service stress
intensity, without reconstructing the crack population. **Not achieved:**
acquisition of the contact, measurement, component-model or nondestructive
load premises for a real specimen. New physical mechanism, practical method
advantage and world novelty are not established.

The result is narrower than the original preload hypothesis. Open-minus-
closed differential compliance is an existing measurement. The useful
extension constructed here retains nonzero closed-contact compliance and
turns it into an explicit radius-dependent sensitivity, rather than treating
compression as a pristine reference.

## Constructed operation

Use the peer's tension/bending convention: p=(p0,p1), stress p0+p1*r,
r=2z/H, and v(r)=(1,r). Let beta=16(1-nu²)/(3E). A circular finite disk
has the open matrix

    C_open/beta = a³ [[1,r],[r,r²+(8/15)(a/H)²]].

The positive a⁵ term is the crack's own bending extent. The peer has
corrected its physical convention and can retain this term conservatively.
I independently obtained it both by opening-displacement integration and
by integrating the primary uniform/bending energy-release rates. The
underlying source is the infinite-medium penny-crack solution of
[Nishioka et al.2008](https://doi.org/10.1299/jcst.2.34), including its
visually checked bending Eq60. This is not a finite-component correction.

Suppose every crack is open at the positive preload and its compressed
normal-contact operator obeys K>=kI, with k>0 supplied in Pa/m. A variational
projection of the ordinary resolvent identity gives the lower contrast

    (C_open-C_compressed)/beta >= h_k(a) v(r)v(r)^T,
    h_k(a)=a³ * beta*k*a/(pi+beta*k*a).

This derivation does not require rigid closure, a minimum crack size, or a
contact solve for every flaw. h_k is increasing. If an error-corrected
measured upper matrix U bounds the sum of these contact-weighted matrices,
every individual crack satisfies

    h_k(a) <= 1/[v(r)^T U^-1 v(r)].

Invert this scalar law, cap the radius geometrically, and maximize the
ordinary affine disk rim intensity over depth. `contact_certificate.py`
does this with rational interval bounds. `PRIMARY_PROOF.md` gives the
